title: Two Ideas, One Sentence
label: ch:fr-joiners
canDo: I can name the order a French sentence holds to, and join two thoughts with and, or, but and because.

payoff.summary: Every verb the book owns is given a reason. The chapter also names the sentence shape the reader has been building for thirty-odd chapters without being told what it was, and says why French is stricter about word order than Latin ever was: Latin's endings said who did what, French wore them off, and position had to take the job.
payoff.note: et was glue in two practice dialogues and never a word; ou is the third pair the accent keeps apart, after a/a-grave and la/la-grave; and parce que closes SPINE-SAY-WHY's only omission.
